newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares driven higher by Lek.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares driven higher by Lek.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 1.34 percent on Thursday in what traders said was largely a technical rebound after recent losses, helped by a strong performance of drug maker Lek's A issue.
"It seems like our market has finally bottomed out," said Andrej Potocnik, a trader at brokerage BPH, but warned that the market would likely continue to see some volatile trading.
The SBI index rose 16.91 points or 1.34 percent to 1,277.69. This index was down 3.29 percent on the week.

Turnover continued to dwindle amid a lack of foreign participation, falling to 50.4 million tolars from 69.3 million. Overall eight shares rose, four fell and three were unchanged, while 11 were untraded.
"I don't think there'll be any major increase in volume or prices until foreigners return to buying," Potocnik said.
Lek's A issue was the most active, jumping 5.38 percent to 23,890 tolars on volume of 1,284 shares for total turnover of 29.8 million tolars.
Warehouse and shopping centre operator BTC, was the biggest gainer, surging 5.69 percent to 13,000 tolars on volume of 535 shares for total turnover of 6.9 million.
Ordinary shares of Dolenjska Bank led the day's decliners, slumping 5.24 percent to 14,110 tolars on volume of 93 shares.
